Thanks Marissa — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Call origin: primarily server-side (our backend APIs). We may experiment with lightweight client-side calls for in-editor suggestions, but those will be rate-limited and lower-privilege.
- Traffic shape: expect 2–3M user-visible queries/month initially, spiking during business hours. Rerank jobs are batched; roughly ~200k/month rerank calls initially.
- Latency: 200ms p50 is a fair bar for the quick UI flows; p95 can be relaxed to ~800ms for non-critical tasks.
- Region: primary in us-east (us-east-1), but we need failover to us-west/eu in case of regional incidents.
- Cost: procurement will push for a predictable per-request estimate; we're open to a pilot to validate numbers.

On routing/policy: we like the idea of using a faster (and more expensive) model for interactive reads and falling back to a cheaper model for bulk/batch reranks. Can you share how Redwood recommends defining the fallback chain and region-based routing (policy snippets or examples would be helpful).

I'll loop in our procurement person if/when we get to pricing. For now, Marcus' technical follow-up will be most useful.

Best,
Samir

Hi Samir / Elena —

Following up with a sketch of the integration and some concrete suggestions for routing/policy based on the targets you shared. High level first, then a short example policy and test plan.

1) SDK + auth - Server-side SDK usage is recommended: calls originate from Acme backend services to Redwood endpoints. Use API keys stored in your KMS; for Private deployments we can add mTLS and customer-managed KMS. - For client-side/embedded calls, use a proxy service in your backend that enforces rate limits and strips any PII before calling the model.

2) Model routing & policy (recommendation) - Primary route: low-latency model (routed to GPU-backed pool in us-east) for interactive UI flows with SLO p50 <= 200ms. - Fallback chain: when latency/SLO cannot be met (e.g., queue depth high) or cost mode is set to "economy", fallback to a CPU-quantized model or smaller variant in the same region. - Region failover: prefer local region (us-east), but on sustained degradation switch to us-west then eu with stateful KV cache warm-up plan (prefetch common prompts).

Example policy snippet (pseudoconfig):
- route: interactive
  prefer: model-x-gpu
  latency_slo_ms: 200
  fallback_chain: [model-x-cpu-quant, model-y-small]
  region_preference: [us-east, us-west, eu]
- route: batch-rerank
  prefer: model-y-small
  cost_mode: economy
  batch_window_ms: 5000
  region_preference: [us-east]

3) Embeddings + reranker - Recommendation: host vector index in the same region as query traffic (us-east). Use a lightweight embedder for candidate recall (cheaper), run a reranker with a stronger model for top-K (K=8–16). - To save cost, run embed-only recall asynchronously for bulk jobs and rerank only the top N synchronously.

4) Caching & prefix awareness - Cache recent KV cache and common prompt prefixes at the routing/edge layer to reduce token costs and latency.

5) Test plan - Staging: run a small synthetic workload (50k queries/day) with canary routing to validate p50/p95 targets and the fallback behavior.
- Metrics: token cost per request, p50/p95 latency, fallback-rate percentage, model-quality regression on a 100-case eval set.

I've attached an updated integration diagram and sample-api-config.yaml that maps the policy to a simple SDK call pattern. Happy to walk through these in a short call — propose Tue or Wed next week.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
